title: a-rehearsal-stands-over-the-design-not-the-cursor
intention: A clean rehearsal record stands over the ticket's DESIGN, so the cursor moving through the workflow does not make it stale; any edit to the design still does.
why: Measured three times (2026-09-17, 09-24, 10-01): the BUILDME crossing's cursor write stales the clean rehearsal that admitted it, so the crossing out of BUILDME refuses until a second cold read of the unchanged design. The lived symptom: every voyage stalls at BUILDME for 5-12 minutes and pays twice for the same reading.
traces_to: Law 1: re-reading a design whose bytes did not change is re-deriving the settled. Akien's review bandwidth and cost (memory akiens-review-bandwidth-is-the-binding-constraint): every voyage pays a duplicate cold read today. The entry gate's purpose (ticket buildme-rides-the-rehearsal): the design was rehearsed clean over the bytes the build reads; the cursor is not something the build reads.
how: In cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py add design_sha(blob): the sha256 of the ticket JSON with its workflow_and_state and rehearsal keys removed, serialized with sort_keys. A clean record carries design_sha256 beside ticket_sha256. standing() is ok when the record's design_sha256 equals design_sha of the live bytes, or (for records written before this) when ticket_sha256 equals the whole-bytes sha as today. Proved by a new proof cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_design_sha.py over a fixture commons.
falsifier: RED if over a fixture commons: (1) a clean record goes stale when only workflow_and_state changes; (2) it stays ok when any other field (a decision, the how) changes; (3) a pre-change record whose ticket_sha256 matches the live bytes stops standing; (4) a clean pass's record lacks design_sha256. Horizon: the tester seal.
watchme: none, because the consumer is the BUILDME entry lane buildme_rides_the_rehearsal in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py, which reads standing() at every crossing into and out of BUILDME
children: none, because the change is one helper and one comparison in cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py plus its proof
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) design_sha? def design_sha(blob: bytes) -> str: doc = json.loads(blob); doc.pop('workflow_and_state', None); doc.pop('rehearsal', None); return _sha(json.dumps(doc, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8')). (2) Where written? In the clean branch after the pointer write, record['design_sha256'] = design_sha(live); for an unclean pass, design_sha of the bytes read. (3) standing()? after the clean check: if rec.get('design_sha256'): stale iff it != design_sha(blob); else fall back to the ticket_sha256 compare unchanged; the stale lack text is kept. (4) Proof? a fixture commons dir with tickets/<id>-x.json and rehearsals/<rec>.json written by hand, standing(id, root=fixture) asserted per tooth.

decisions.text: STEP 1, the red proof, measured 2026-10-01. Write cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_design_sha.py, runnable as a script. Fixtures are NOT re-invented: import World, Stub, CLEAN_TREE, TID and _kw from the sibling proof (from cairn.machines.rehearsal.proofs.test_rehearsal import ...; proofs/ has no __init__.py and imports as a namespace package). World() builds a scratch commons (scratch_dir('rehearsal-proof-')) with tickets/, rehearsals/, questions/ and the fixture ticket TID, and points the artifact door at it; w.close() in finally. Resolve the machine as R = importlib.import_module('cairn.machines.rehearsal.rehearsal') INSIDE each tooth, and read design_sha via getattr(R, 'design_sha') there, so a reverted build reds teeth instead of crashing the import. Each tooth first makes a clean record with rec = R.rehearse(TID, reader=Stub([CLEAN_TREE]), **_kw(w)) and asserts R.standing(TID, w.commons)['ok']. Teeth: test_a_cursor_move_leaves_the_record_standing (rewrite the ticket through door.write(str(w.ticket), ..., verb='cast', why='fixture cursor move') with only workflow_and_state changed from [BUILDME:waiting] to [PROVEME]: standing ok stays True); test_a_design_edit_makes_the_record_stale (same, but append a decision {'n': 3, 'text': 'a new decision', 'by': 'the proof'}: standing ok is False and its lack is 'the ticket was edited after its rehearsal — rehearse again'); test_a_pre_change_record_still_stands_on_the_whole_bytes (load the record at w.commons / rec['record'], drop design_sha256, write it back through door.write(..., verb='rehearse', why='fixture pre-change record'): standing ok is True while the ticket bytes are unchanged, and False after a workflow_and_state-only edit, because an old record falls back to the whole-bytes compare); test_a_clean_record_carries_design_sha256 (rec['design_sha256'] == R.design_sha(w.ticket.read_bytes())). PROVES = {'9fb045a476dc': {'1': 'test_a_cursor_move_leaves_the_record_standing', '2': 'test_a_design_edit_makes_the_record_stale', '3': 'test_a_pre_change_record_still_stands_on_the_whole_bytes', '4': 'test_a_clean_record_carries_design_sha256'}}. main() runs every tooth whatever the one before did and prints PASS/FAIL lines, exactly as test_rehearsal.py main() does. Run red: teeth 1 and 4 fail; 2 and 3 may pass before the build, which is expected.

STEP 2, the build in cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py. (a) Beside _sha (line 118): def design_sha(blob: bytes) -> str: doc = json.loads(blob); doc.pop('workflow_and_state', None); doc.pop('rehearsal', None); return _sha(json.dumps(doc, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8')). (b) In the record-writing block (line ~480): in the clean branch, after live = _write_ticket(...), design = design_sha(live); in the unclean branch design = design_sha of the bytes read (the blob whose sha is sha_at_read); the record dict gains 'design_sha256': design right after 'ticket_sha256_at_read'. (c) In standing() (line 558), replace the single ticket_sha256 compare with: if rec.get('design_sha256'): stale = rec['design_sha256'] != design_sha(blob) else: stale = rec.get('ticket_sha256') != _sha(blob); on stale return the same dict as today (same lack text, ticket_sha256 and live_sha256 keys); on ok return today's dict plus 'design_sha256': rec.get('design_sha256'). Update standing()'s docstring to say design, not bytes. (d) Run test_design_sha.py green twice, then test_rehearsal.py, which must stay green (its tooth 3 asserts a stale hash reds — check it edits a design field; if it edits only workflow_and_state, that tooth's fixture edit moves to a decision field in the same build, because it is this component's proof). build_inspector's docstring at cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py:2139 says ticket_sha256: another component, not edited here (RULE 1); its sieve reads R.standing and keeps working because the return keys are unchanged.

D1's ticket edit, exact syntax, the same shape test_rehearsal.py uses at line 315-317 (door is 'from cairn.tools.artifact import artifact as door', imported at module top like the sibling's line 69). For the cursor move: doc = json.loads(w.ticket.read_text()); doc['workflow_and_state'] = doc['workflow_and_state'].replace('[BUILDME:waiting]', 'BUILDME').replace('-> PROVEME ->', '-> [PROVEME] ->'); door.write(str(w.ticket), json.dumps(doc, indent=2) + '
', verb='cast', why='fixture cursor move'). The fixture ticket's workflow_and_state is 'code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [BUILDME:waiting] -> PROVEME -> PROVED' (test_rehearsal.py line 99), so after the edit it reads 'code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> [PROVEME] -> PROVED'; assert that exact string before asserting standing, so a no-op replace cannot read as a pass. For the design edit: doc = json.loads(w.ticket.read_text()); doc['decisions'].append({'n': 3, 'text': 'a new decision', 'by': 'the proof'}); door.write(str(w.ticket), json.dumps(doc, indent=2) + '
', verb='cast', why='fixture design edit'). For the pre-change record: p = w.commons / rec['record']; d = json.loads(p.read_text()); d.pop('design_sha256', None); door.write(str(p), json.dumps(d, indent=2) + '
', verb='rehearse', why='fixture pre-change record'). standing is called as R.standing(TID, w.commons).
